near_term_decision.existing_capability: Procedural store(array,index,value), store(scalar_ref,value), and setfield(record_ref,field,value) already perform persistent writes and return the stored value. Parenthesized value-argument operations can dispatch to procedures under current bindings.
near_term_decision.candidate_a: Define array-element and regional-field assignment as source sugar for the existing write operations. Do not add a first-class assignable-location object or a separate assignment method family.
near_term_decision.candidate_b: Give assignment its own compiler operation and overload family. Its operand/reference and field-selection contracts would need explicit design before implementation.
near_term_decision.recommendation: Prefer candidate A if the next requirement is only more convenient regional writes. Candidate B needs a demonstrated behavior that existing write dispatch cannot express.
shared_constraints: A symbolic variable still changes only via effect; @x = value remains invalid.
Writes remain procedural and obey the existing owning-region lifetime.
The left-hand receiver/index and right-hand expression must each execute once in a specified order.
Preserve each selected argument conversion before evaluating the next argument.
Field syntax must not silently introduce field-name runtime values or metadata.
not_selected: Assignment precedence, associativity and expression result grammar

naming_boundary.status: pending human choice; current behavior reproduced, no grammar change
naming_boundary.observed: function type(x::i64)::i64 { x + 1 } and function using(...) are accepted; calls inside @print arguments check successfully, but type(7); and using(7); at module top level are consumed as declaration/resource syntax and fail.
naming_boundary.candidate_a: Reserve primary module-form words type, regional, unit, array, using, import and conversion against ordinary declarations. Keep field selectors and @symbol tokens contextual.
naming_boundary.candidate_b: Keep those names contextual and distinguish a top-level call from its declaration form by grammar/lookahead.
naming_boundary.recommendation: Candidate A gives a consistent small keyword set and early declaration diagnostics. Candidate B preserves currently accepted nested uses but requires a contextual module grammar.
naming_boundary.authority: H-153 requires a reserved keyword set but does not confirm this expanded inventory; H-160 defers the new choice.
